newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac says firms must do their part for jobs.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says firms must do their part for jobs.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac attacked French companies on Friday, saying they should stop complaining and play their part in creating jobs in France.

One of the responsibilities of a company is to "stop complaining, clearly identify problems and do everything to build confidence and in particular to create growth," Chirac said on a visit to southern France.

"The state will not fix everything. We will not fix employment by recruiting civil servants. We will solve the employment problem by creating (favourable) economic conditions," he said at a conference on jobs for young people.

France remains bedevilled by record 12.7 percent unemployment, which Chirac pledged during his presidential campaign to lower. The centre-right government has also recently begun a crusade to lower youth unemployment, which stands at 25 percent.

It was not the first time Chirac has taken a shot at French companies. A year ago, while on a trip to Singapore, Chirac said French banks were "badly managed" and a "cause for despair". In January 1996, he blasted French companies for not doing enough to create jobs.

Banks have rejected the charges and criticised the president for publicly attacking French business. "It's as if (British Prime Minister) John Major went to Paris and said all English banks were useless," a banker said after Chirac's outburst in Singapore.

On Friday, the head of state said that not only companies were to blame. "Excessive, abusive and paralysing administrative constraints" increased French companies' reluctance to hire new workers, and these constraints must be loosened, he said.
Chirac again singled out French banks for criticism, saying they were not willing enough to help young people start businesses.
"It is frustrating to see that young people who have been helped, who have a reasonable plan, almost never find a bank to trust them...we have to fix this," he said.
